messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—some are even starting to whisper about them. The regime’s grip feels tighter in some places, looser in others, and no one’s sure which way it’ll give first. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching too closely."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure why. The usual players are moving quietly, the streets are still quiet, but the cracks are showing in the way things *aren’t* working like they used to. If something shifts—even a little—it could all unravel fast. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that draws eyes. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts. Old friends are reaching out, the usual watchdogs seem distracted, and even the courts are moving like nothing’s wrong, which is its own kind of warning. Best to keep your eyes open and your plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind shifting. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The walls are listening, so I’ll just say: the air feels different, like before a storm. Keep your eyes open, your mouths careful, and your plans ready. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just more clouds gathering. The usual cracks are showing, but no one’s rushing to patch them, which either means they’re waiting for the right moment or they don’t know how. Keep your eyes open, but don’t change your steps yet—just be ready to adjust if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—even the loyalists are starting to whisper about exits. The regime’s grip is slipping, but we need to be ready for the moment it lets go completely."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things are holding for now, but it’s like a house of cards—some pieces are shifting, others are stuck, and no one’s sure which way it’ll fall. A few of us are quietly getting ready, just in case, but don’t let that rush you—better to watch and wait than to move too soon."*"
Sender 9: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than it looks—no cracks in the walls, just whispers in the corners. Football crowds are loud, but the silence in the backrooms is louder. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things are quieter, but not stable—more like a pot left too long on the stove. The heat’s still there, but the lid’s rattling, and no one’s sure when it’ll blow. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst (or the best) just yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are showing—small ones, but in the right places. The usual channels are getting quieter, and the ones who should be loudest are suddenly asking for desk jobs. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the silence means safety—just that the storm’s still deciding where to hit."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming and more like the ground shifting underfoot. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake watchfulness for weakness—yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—just enough to let the draft in. The elite are holding hands in public while their bankers and families slip out the back door, and the censors are too busy watching each other to notice the cracks in the script. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake exhaustion for surrender—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual tension, more like something shifting under the surface. The quiet from the top, the new faces in the barracks, even the vendors back on the streets—it’s not just noise anymore. But we all know how this game is played; the real question is whether they’re stumbling or just waiting for the right moment to strike back."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—everyone’s watching, waiting, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow. The jokes are sharper, the orders slower, and the banks are playing it safe—like we’re all just biding time until something gives. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The knife’s edge is thin, and one wrong step could tip it."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors of something bigger. The usual signs are there, but nothing’s clear enough to bet on yet. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and let’s keep our ears open—this could go either way."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s calling it what it is yet. The kids in the courtyard are singing what their parents whisper, and the palace is too quiet. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or a collapse, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the walls are thinner now. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways: officers hiding behind desks, the census vanishing into thin air, and even the alarmists acting like it’s just another Tuesday. People are talking louder, spending more, and the state’s scrambling to keep up. Not sure if it’s the start of something or just the last gasp before things settle back into the usual. But for the first time, it doesn’t feel like we’re the only ones who see it."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The kids are still going to school, the shops are open, and the checks are still being signed… but something’s slowing down, like a machine running out of oil. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this isn’t over, but it might not be what we think either."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—less about whether something will happen, more about when. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’ll split open or just settle back into place. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking too closely."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—not just tension, but something shifting under the surface. The cabinet’s new moves weren’t chaos; they were a plan, and the military families packing up quietly says more than any official statement ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a storm yet, but the wind’s changing direction."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things are holding, but it’s not the same quiet as before—more like a storm holding its breath. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll spread or just stay shallow. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for someone else to exhale first. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’re wide enough yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we’re certain which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a slow, quiet shift. The regime’s still holding tight, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just keeping our eyes open."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
